1 --- 2 title: prefetch 3 description: API reference for the prefetch route segment config. 4 related: 5 title: Next Steps 6 description: Learn how to use instant navigations in practice. 7 links: 8 - app/guides/instant-navigation 9 - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant 10 --- 11 12 The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. To override per segment, set this export to one of the values below. 13 14 > **Good to know**: 15 > 16 > - The `prefetch` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled. 17 > - `prefetch` cannot be used when the segment is a Client Component. 18 > - The meaningful values to set are `'partial'` and `'force-disabled'`. `'auto'` is the default and is equivalent to omitting the export; don't write `prefetch = 'auto'` explicitly. 19 20 ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher 21 export const prefetch = 'partial' 22 23 export default function Page() { 24 return
...
25 } 26 ``` 27 28 ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher 29 export const prefetch = 'partial' 30 31 export default function Page() { 32 return
...
33 } 34 ``` 35 36 ## Options 37 38 ### `'partial'` 39 40 Opts the segment into [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) without enabling the global [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) flag. A `` pointing at a segment with `prefetch = 'partial'` loads the per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) instead of the legacy full prefetch. Set this on the destination, not the link. 41 42 For links that opt into a wider prefetch with [``](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), Next.js uses per-link prefetching. The server renders a fresh response that resolves URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL). On pages where all the content is statically renderable, Next.js serves prefetches from the static cache. If a page accesses non-static data, it's prefetched at runtime. 43 44 Use this for incremental adoption when you can't enable `partialPrefetching` for the entire app at once. Once every route in scope has `prefetch = 'partial'`, enable the global flag and remove the per-route exports. 45 46 > **Good to know**: When Next.js performs a per-link prefetch for a segment, all downstream segments are included in the same request. Segments deeper in the tree that are configured with `'force-disabled'` will still be prefetched as part of the response. 47 48 ```tsx filename="page.tsx" 49 export const prefetch = 'partial' 50 ``` 51 52 ### `'force-disabled'` 53 54 Never prefetch this segment. The client will not request segment data ahead of navigation. Use this for segments where prefetching would be wasteful, for example pages behind authentication that are rarely visited. 55 56 > **Good to know**: `'force-disabled'` does not prevent Next.js from prefetching metadata about the route. However, the actual segment data for this segment and all deeper segments will be omitted from prefetching. 57 58 ## Relationship with the `` prop 59 60 A prefetch starts with a `` that expresses intent (should this destination be prefetched, and how eagerly), and ends at a segment that sets a cost ceiling (how much work is it OK to do ahead of time, for any link that points here). 61 62 A destination can't know which links target it, so the segment config caps what any `` pulls: 63 64 - [`'partial'`](#partial): App Shell for default links; a `` additionally resolves URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL) and the cached content behind it. 65 - [`'force-disabled'`](#force-disabled): skip segment data entirely. 66 67 `` skips prefetching at the link level regardless of how the destination is configured. 68 69 > **Good to know**: On pages where all the content is statically renderable, Next.js serves prefetches from the static cache (or a CDN). If a page accesses non-static data like cookies or headers, it's prefetched at runtime with a fresh server render, which costs server CPU per page view. 70 71 ## TypeScript 72 73 ```tsx 74 type Prefetch = 'auto' | 'partial' | 'force-disabled' 75 76 export const prefetch: Prefetch = 'partial' 77 ``` 78 79 ## Version History 80 81 | Version | Changes | 82 | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | 83 | `v16.x.x` | `prefetch` export introduced (Cache Components only) | 84

Use it to verify that your loading states look right, confirm the content you expect appears immediately, and iterate on where to place `` boundaries. 241 242 The [React DevTools Suspense panel](https://react.dev/learn/react-developer-tools) complements this: it lists the `` boundaries in the tree and lets you toggle each one between its fallback and resolved state, so you can see exactly which boundary covers which part of the page. 243 244 {/* TODO: screenshot — React DevTools Suspense panel listing boundaries with toggle controls */} 245 246 The Navigation Inspector is available when Cache Components is enabled: 247 248 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4} 249 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 250 251 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 252 cacheComponents: true, 253 } 254 255 export default nextConfig 256 ``` 257 258 Open the Next.js DevTools and select **Navigation Inspector**, then toggle **Pause on navigations**. The panel shows **Awaiting navigation...** With the toggle on, the next refresh or link click freezes the page so you can inspect the shell. 259 260 Refresh the product page. The Inspector freezes and shows **Loading shell** labeled **Page load** with the target URL. In the app, two fallbacks appear: "Loading product..." and "Checking availability...". On the first visit the cache is cold and both are visible. 261 262

The Inspector shows **Loading shell** labeled **Client nav** with both source and target URLs. In the app, the product name and price appear immediately (cached). "Checking availability..." shows where inventory will stream in. 285 286

Each navigation pauses as long as the toggle is on. 307 308 > **Good to know:** Page loads and client navigations can produce different shells. Client-side hooks like `useSearchParams` suspend on page loads (search params are not known at build time) but resolve synchronously on client navigations (the router already has the params). 309 310 ## Prevent regressions with e2e tests 311 312 Validation catches structural problems during development, but as the codebase grows, the structural checks can only tell you that a shell exists. They can't tell you whether the right content is in it. E2E tests close that gap: they assert on what the user actually sees when the navigation completes, catching regressions before they ship. 313 314 The [`@next/playwright`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@next/playwright) package includes an `instant()` helper for this. Install it alongside `@playwright/test`: 315 316 ```bash package="pnpm" 317 pnpm add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test 318 ``` 319 320 ```bash package="npm" 321 npm install -D @next/playwright @playwright/test 322 ``` 323 324 ```bash package="yarn" 325 yarn add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test 326 ``` 327 328 ```bash package="bun" 329 bun add -D @next/playwright @playwright/test 330 ``` 331 332 A route can be reached two ways, and a `` boundary can cover one without covering the other: 333 334 - **Initial page load**: Use `page.goto()` to test the static UI from the document response. 335 - **Client navigation**: Click a `` to test the destination's prefetched UI. [Per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) can add request-specific content to this UI. 336 337 ```typescript filename="e2e/navigation.test.ts" highlight={6-14,20-25} 338 import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test' 339 import { instant } from '@next/playwright' 340 341 test.describe('Product page (/store/[slug])', () => { 342 test('is instant on an initial page load', async ({ page, baseURL }) => { 343 await instant( 344 page, 345 async () => { 346 await page.goto('/store/hats') 347 await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap') 348 await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toHaveCount(0) 349 }, 350 { baseURL } 351 ) 352 await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toBeVisible() 353 }) 354 355 test('is instant on a client navigation', async ({ page }) => { 356 await page.goto('/store/shoes') 357 await instant(page, async () => { 358 await page.click('a[href="/store/hats"]') 359 await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === '/store/hats') 360 await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap') 361 await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toHaveCount(0) 362 }) 363 await expect(page.getByText('In stock')).toBeVisible() 364 }) 365 }) 366 ``` 367 368 Pass Playwright's `baseURL` to `instant()` when `page.goto()` is the first navigation. The helper needs the origin before requesting the document. 369 370 Inside the callback, an initial page load shows the static UI and a client navigation shows the destination's prefetched UI. Other dynamic content remains blocked until the callback finishes. 371 372 > **Good to know:** The start of the `instant()` scope is the same as turning on **Pause on navigations** in the Navigation Inspector, and the end of the scope releases the pause the way **Resume** does. 373 374 For client navigations, wait for the destination URL before asserting on its UI. Otherwise, a shared selector can match the source page before the destination commits. If the prefetched destination cannot commit, the URL wait times out and the test fails. 375 376 Run these against `next dev`, where the testing API is enabled automatically. To run them in CI against a production build, set `exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild` so `next start` exposes the same API: 377 378 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5} 379 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 380 381 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 382 cacheComponents: true, 383 experimental: { exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild: true }, 384 } 385 386 export default nextConfig 387 ``` 388 389 Focus these tests on the user flows that matter most. 390 391 ## Fixing a navigation that blocks 392 393 Consider a different route, `/products/[slug]`, that fetches product data from a public API and shows a featured list alongside: 394 395 ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx" 396 export default async function ProductPage( 397 props: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'> 398 ) { 399 const featured = await getFeatured() 400 const { slug } = await props.params 401 const res = await fetch(`https://next-recipe-api.vercel.dev/products/${slug}`) 402 const product = await res.json() 403 404 return ( 405

The featured list ships with the App Shell. 510 511 > **Good to know:** In serverless deployments, in-memory caching with `"use cache"` will not persist across instances. Consider using [`"use cache: remote"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) for persistent caching. 512 513 Validation passes. Open the DevTools and try a client navigation. The featured section appears immediately, and **"Loading product..."** shows where the product details will stream in. 514 515 ### Iterate on loading states 516 517 {/* TODO: diagram — before/after illustration showing a single high-up Suspense boundary being refined down to smaller boundaries closer to the data */} 518 519 Validation passing means the navigation is instant. It does not mean the loading states are good. A `` boundary placed high in the tree (say, wrapping the whole page) might satisfy validation, but it replaces most of the page with a single fallback on every navigation. 520 521 The best loading states keep as much real, cached content visible as possible and only show fallbacks where data is actually in flight. A product page that keeps the header, image, and description visible with only the price and availability behind a fallback feels faster than a full-page skeleton, even at the same total load time. 522 523 Use the [DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) to see what your users see, or see the [AI workflow](#ai-workflow) for automating the loop with an agent. 524 525 ## AI workflow 526 527 At a high level, an agent optimizes a single navigation like this: 528 529 - **Observe**: read validation insights and choose the exact navigation and UI that should appear immediately. 530 - **Test**: confirm the target UI renders normally, then write an `instant()` test and verify that it fails before changing the route. 531 - **Fix**: validation errors name a specific component and suggest a fix (`use cache` or ``). The agent applies the fix and re-runs validation. 532 - **Verify**: run the test against a production-like build and keep the passing test as a regression guard. 533 534 The agent doesn't need to understand the full caching model, only to follow the insights and errors until they're gone. It does need your app-specific intent, though. Tell it what should appear immediately, what can stream in, and what must stay fresh. When a caching decision is unclear, keep the data fresh behind `` rather than guessing a cache lifetime. 535 536 For [iterating on loading states](#iterate-on-loading-states), a prompt like "maximize my content, and reduce the amount that needs to be behind a spinner" works well for pushing boundaries down. 537 538 Agents working on a Cache Components route typically reach for three levers: 539 540 - **Push down**: extract I/O into a Suspense-wrapped child so the parent stays static and static siblings lift into the shell. 541 - **Cache**: pair `'use cache'` with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) to assign a freshness profile. 542 - **Per-link prefetching** (nav-only): when a route reads URL data (`searchParams` or `params`), opt it into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) so the framework resolves that data at link-prefetch time. Session data from `cookies()` or `headers()` already lands in the App Shell without it. 543 544 Each refactor should pair with a before/after capture to verify the change actually landed. Identical-looking captures mean the refactor didn't take effect. 545 546 For agents to see what their changes actually render, pair this with [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser). With React DevTools enabled it reports the component tree and which `` boundaries are still pending, so an agent can make a change, snapshot the shell, check what landed, and adjust. See [Runtime visibility](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#step-2-give-agents-runtime-visibility) in the AI agents guide for the setup. 547 548 The [`next-cache-components-optimizer`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-cache-components-optimizer) Skill packages this loop. It confirms the target UI renders normally, writes an `instant()` test that fails before the fix, then works it to green against a production-like build and ships it as a regression guard. Use it for the initial load (hard navigation), client-side navigation (soft navigation), or both. 549 550 ## Opting out 551 552 Not every layout or page can or should be instant. When the structural fix isn't worth the work, or when a route isn't a priority for instant navigation, refine validation at one of two scopes. 553 554 The dev overlay surfaces this as the **Block** fix alongside every insight: 555 556 557 566 567 568 Set `instant = false` on the page or layout file. This opts the segment out of validation feedback. The segment may still navigate instantly if its structure supports it; the framework just won't surface insights for it. Navigations between sibling segments below are still validated. 569 570 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 571 export const instant = false 572 ``` 573 574 With `false` on `/dashboard/layout.tsx`, validation no longer flags navigations into `/dashboard` from outside; navigations between `/dashboard/a` and `/dashboard/b` are still checked. 575 576 For opted-out segments, the navigation blocks on the server. If the content depends on cookies or headers but has a known cache lifetime, caching it with [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) lets the App Shell carry it ahead of the click instead of opting out, as long as its [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) time is at least 5 minutes. 577 578 ## Next steps 579 580 - [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the recommended `` defaults and a step-by-step adoption path 581 - [`instant` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) for the full configuration 582 - [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when parts of your route depend on URL data (`searchParams` or `params`) and should resolve before navigation 583 - [Caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) for background on `use cache`, Suspense, and Partial Prerendering 584 - [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating) for how to expire cached data with `cacheLife` and `updateTag` 585

Fixed. The product page's title now appears instantly on navigation, with the inventory streaming in behind it.

**What was wrong:** `app/product/page.tsx` awaited `getInventory()` at the top of the page component. That function calls `connection()`, which forces it to run at request time on every visit — and because the whole page waited on it, nothing (not even the static "Premium Widget" heading) could render until the server responded. With `cacheComponents: true` enabled in this Next.js 16.4 setup, that means no static shell existed for the route, so client navigations from home blocked entirely.

**The fix** (per the instant-navigation guide in this version's bundled docs, `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/instant-navigation.md`): I moved the data fetch into an async `<Inventory />` child component and wrapped it in a `<Suspense>` boundary with a "Checking availability..." fallback. The page component itself is now fully static, so the title and fallback become part of the prerendered shell that's prefetched for the `<Link>` on the home page. I kept the inventory uncached rather than using `'use cache'`, since stock counts should stay fresh on each request.

The build confirms it: `/product` now shows as `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content — where previously it would have been fully dynamic. Navigation renders the title immediately, and the stock count and price stream into the fallback when the server responds.
